title: Refactor CI workflows: consolidate matrices and bump Actions/tooling dependencies
author: Alexandra Cho
description: Motivation: our repo CI had grown organically into many slightly different matrices across services and SDKs which doubled similar runner combinations, increased queue time, and amplified flaky failure surface. This PR collapses duplicate axes into a single reusable matrix template, bumps key GitHub Actions and setup tooling to current stable releases, tightens conditional execution to avoid unnecessary jobs on docs-only and infra-only changes, and rationalizes Dependabot config. Changes include: extract .github/workflows/templates/ci-matrix.yml and reuse across SDK and core workflows; move runner/os/version axes into a single matrix with include/strategies for platform-specific jobs; upgrade actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/setup-python@v4, docker/build-push-action@v4; pin several internal composite actions and add a lightweight warmup job to reduce cold-start latency on self-hosted runners; add a retry wrapper for the flakiest integration test step; reduce redundant builds by ~38% on average; update release workflow to use a single release template that supports both nightly and tagged releases; update dependabot to ignore transient devtools that conflict with CI runners. Linear refs: ENG-4123 for matrix consolidation, ENG-4188 for CI flakiness; this PR also addresses part of OPS-734 (release automation reliability). Checklist: 1) CI templates added and referenced in core and SDK workflows; 2) Action versions bumped and pinned; 3) Conditional path filters added; 4) Dependabot tuned; 5) Manual smoke run performed and stable for 48h. Rollout: squash-merged to main and monitored for two days with alert thresholds lowered for job latency. Notes: no runtime behavior changes, only CI infra and tooling; teams with local CI assumptions should read .github/README-ci.md for the new matrix semantics and reuse patterns.

release_notes: CI: Consolidated multiple workflow matrices into a single reusable template; upgraded key GitHub Actions to v4; added retry wrapper for flaky integration step; reduced CI job count by ~38% and improved self-hosted runner warm-starts; updated Dependabot to reduce noisy devtool bumps.
motivating_issue: CI queue time spikes and frequent transient failures in nightly runs increased developer wait time and blocked release automation. This refactor reduces duplicated runner combinations and targets root causes for flake amplification.
rationale: Consolidating duplicate axes and centralizing job templates reduces maintenance surface, enforces consistent tooling versions across the monorepo, and reduces cost and latency. Pinning and digesting third-party actions improves reproducibility. Conditional runs avoid unnecessary compute for docs-only edits.
notes_for_ops: After merge: 1) monitor job queue length metric ci.runner.queue_seconds for 72h; 2) if self-hosted runners show >20% cold-starts, adjust warmup concurrency in scripts/ci/warmup-runner.sh; 3) follow up with Dependabot PRs for remaining action bumps and pin digests as required.
